A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same multimodal protein language model design-space study. Their main text, equations, eight figures, nineteen tables, and Appendices A–E are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original tokenizer reconstruction, protein folding, generation, and multimer experiments, with additional inverse-folding, representation-learning, and ablation results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental outcomes in the main text and Appendix D, including results for the proposed DPLM-2 variants.

M1.justification: Sections 3–6 and Appendix C retain the same ResDiff, bitwise modeling, hybrid flow-based sampling, GeoDPLM, representation alignment, and multimer adaptations. No algorithm, architecture, objective, or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation coverage remains the same, including CAMEO 2022, PDB date split, PDB-Multimer, SwissProt, AFDB Rep, HUMANPPI, and DeepLoc Subcellular. Folding, generation, inverse folding, and representation-learning tasks are retained; the new ProteinBench citation does not introduce an evaluation.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments: Table 4 retains ESMFold, MultiFlow, ESM3, and DPLM-2 comparisons, while Table 14 retains SaProt. Newly cited methods in Appendix E are not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Both versions retain the same splits, metrics, model configurations, training budgets, and testing procedures. Examples include 40 generated samples per protein length and the multimer filtering that yields 3,462 training samples.

E4.justification: The geometry-component ablations in Table 5 and design-combination analysis in Table 7 are unchanged. Appendix D retains the same residual-diffusion case study, alignment analyses, linker/offset sensitivity studies, pretraining comparison, and efficiency analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. Table 8 retains the same descriptive means and spreads for multimer dataset characteristics.

E6.justification: The numerical result entries, plotted findings, and qualitative examples are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 4 retains PDB RMSD 2.3698 for BIT-based DPLM-2 with FM, ResDiff, and folding SFT; Table 14 retains 88.89% HUMANPPI accuracy for DPLM-2 BITWISE.

T1.justification: The probabilistic definitions, diffusion and bitwise objectives, residual-diffusion loss, flow interpolation, and representation-alignment formulation are unchanged. No mathematical assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same bottleneck diagnosis and contributions concerning structural accuracy, generation diversity, and multimer data. The abstract's claimed PDB RMSD reduction from 5.52 to 2.36 for the 650M model is unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of component compatibility and structural refinement remain unchanged. Appendix B retains the same limitations concerning discrete representations, missing physical constraints, scaling, and scarce multimer data; removing redundant prose does not alter these qualifications.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly labels the existing project address as 'Project page and code,' whereas v1 labels it only as a page. This is a limited clarification of code-access information, not evidence of a new release; implementation settings, hardware, and timing disclosures in Appendices C and D.6 remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix E adds five cited works: two diffusion-language-model papers by Ye et al. (2023), Zheng et al. (2023b), ProteinBench, and Chen et al. (2025). Brief additions acknowledge structure-informed models and all-atom protein-complex generation without substantially changing the paper's research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 standardizes several DPLM-2 spellings, corrects 'langauge,' removes a repetitive passage in Appendix B, and lightly expands related work. Affiliations and publication text are updated, and acknowledgements are revised and moved before the impact statement; the scientific narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Typesetting and text flow change modestly, including moving Table 3 from the lower left column to the upper right column on page 4 and revising the first-page footer. All figures and tables retain their content, captions, and display structures.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves scholarly context through the added attribution and all-atom modeling discussion in Appendix E, while removing redundant prose in Appendix B and clarifying the code-access label. The methods, experimental support, results, and substantive limitations remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited to documentation and presentation.
